statement: How many positive integers less than $10000$ are multiples of $9$ and have only odd digits?

choices.misconception: I only counted the four-digit numbers and forgot the shorter ones: $9$, $99$ and the eleven three-digit numbers.
I forgot that four odd digits can also add up to $36$, so I missed $9999$.
I gave every four-digit digit set with a repeated digit $12$ orders, but $\{3, 3, 3, 9\}$ and $\{3, 5, 5, 5\}$ use one digit three times, so they have only $4$ orders each.
I gave each of the seven four-digit digit sets with sum $18$ a full $24$ orders, as if the four digits were always different.

hints: A number is a multiple of $9$ exactly when its digit sum is. Split by the number of digits, and think about whether a sum of odd digits is odd or even.
With $1$ or $3$ odd digits the sum is odd, so it is $9$ or $27$. With $2$ or $4$ odd digits the sum is even, so it is $18$ or $36$. Up to three digits there are $13$ such numbers in all.

For four digits, list the sets of four odd digits with sum $18$, such as $\{1, 3, 5, 9\}$ and $\{1, 1, 7, 9\}$. There are seven sets. Count the orders of each: $24$ if all digits differ, $12$ if one digit appears twice, $4$ if one appears three times.

solutions.reliable: A number is a multiple of $9$ exactly when its digit sum is. One digit: only $9$. Two odd digits: the sum is even and at most $18$, so it is $18$, giving only $99$. Three odd digits: the sum is odd and at most $27$, so it is $9$ or $27$. Sum $27$ gives $999$. Sum $9$ uses the digit sets $\{1, 1, 7\}$ ($3$ orders), $\{1, 3, 5\}$ ($6$ orders) and $\{3, 3, 3\}$ ($1$ order), which is $10$ numbers. So far that is $1 + 1 + 1 + 10 = 13$. Four odd digits: the sum is even and at most $36$, so it is $18$ or $36$. Sum $36$ gives only $9999$. For sum $18$ the digit sets are $\{1, 3, 5, 9\}$ ($24$ orders), $\{1, 1, 7, 9\}$, $\{1, 3, 7, 7\}$, $\{1, 5, 5, 7\}$, $\{3, 3, 5, 7\}$ ($12$ orders each) and $\{3, 3, 3, 9\}$, $\{3, 5, 5, 5\}$ ($4$ orders each), for $24 + 4 \cdot 12 + 2 \cdot 4 = 80$ numbers. In total $13 + 1 + 80 = 94$.
solutions.elegant: Write each odd digit as $2x + 1$ with $0 \le x \le 4$. For four digits with sum $18$, the four values of $x$ add to $7$. Without the limit $x \le 4$ there are $\binom{10}{3} = 120$ solutions; a value of $5$ or more can occur in only one place at a time, and for each of the $4$ places there are $\binom{5}{3} = 10$ such solutions, leaving $120 - 40 = 80$. The same idea gives $\binom{5}{2} = 10$ three-digit numbers with sum $9$. Adding $9$, $99$, $999$ and $9999$ gives $80 + 10 + 4 = 94$.
